name: Lake Russell
type: Clear, undeveloped Savannah River lake; cold Hartwell releases
pool: Full pool 475 ft; stays near full

stripers.doing: Stripers mix with bass on brush piles and points where shad are feeding; birds start showing over bait.
how: With Zoom Swimming Fluke Jr. trailers, or small swimbaits.

bass.doing: 20 to 35 ft around rock and timber on main-lake points, ditches and the mouths of creeks, where bait bunches up.
how: A-rig with Swimming Fluke Jr. where fish feed on shad.

crappie.doing: Crappie hold deep, 15 to 30 ft, on deep docks, brush, bridge pilings and creek channels near the mouths of major creeks.
how: Shoot a jig under deep docks and let it fall until it stops.
Small spoon or minnow worked slowly over brush.
Minnows trolled slowly along creek channels.

stripers.doing: Stripers push up the rivers and creeks with the herring as the water warms through the 50s. The upper lake and river channels hold the most fish.
how: Herring or gizzard shad about 40 ft behind the boards.
Unweighted bait 60 to 120 ft back on slow days.
Creek backs on warm afternoons; points and clay banks are steadier.

bass.doing: Spots move up rocky and clay points toward spawning pockets. They hold on the sides of long points and on rock piles from 5 to 30 ft.
how: A 1/4 oz ball-head swimbait crawled across rocky points.
Ned rig, shaky head or drop shot on the sides of long points.
Jerkbait on windy points and riprap.
Skip points with mushy bottoms; pea gravel and chunk rock hold fish.

crappie.doing: Crappie move from creek mouths toward the middle and backs of creeks onto stumps, laydowns, fish attractors and creek ledges.
how: Longline or spider-rig jigs and minnows through creek channels.
Minnow under a float on laydowns and brush.
Warm afternoons after a few warm days in a row.

stripers.doing: Herring stage up the creeks and stripers school on top for the first couple of hours of light, then settle to 25 to 35 ft in the same areas.
how: Topwater and freelined bluebacks over the herring.
Downline bluebacks at 25 to 35 ft nearby.
A cloudy morning can keep the topwater bite going to mid-morning.

bass.doing: Largemouth bed in pockets in the 60s; spotted bass bed deeper, often 10 to 15 ft, on gravel and flat rock. The full moon pushes waves of fish up.
how: Shaky head, wacky rig or Fluke around beds and the bank between them.
Jerkbait across the points into spawning coves.

crappie.doing: Crappie spawn in the backs of creeks in a few feet of water once it reaches about 62 to 65°F.
how: Float and jig or minnow in 1 to 6 ft.
Double jig rig longlined across the flats.

stripers.doing: The herring spawn on points, clay banks, riprap and marina walls at first light, and stripers crash them. By June they slide to brush on points in 15 to 35 ft, then deeper.
how: Walking bait, popper or wake bait on points and humps.
Herring pitched or freelined to points.
Downlines over brush in 15 to 35 ft.

bass.doing: Bass key on the herring and shad spawn on hard banks at dawn, then move to brush on points and humps as the water heads into the 80s.
how: Topwater or wake bait on clay points, bridges and marina walls.
Underspin, white spinnerbait or Fluke run along walls and riprap.
Drop shot or shaky head on brush in 15 to 25 ft.

crappie.doing: Crappie leave the banks for docks and brush in 10 to 15 ft. Singles and small groups are often the bigger fish.
how: Minnows set just above the brush.

stripers.doing: Trophy water with a 2-fish limit. Fish the first few miles below Hartwell Dam, where cold releases draw them, plus channel edges, points and pockets; or deeper water near Russell Dam. Mornings are steadier; big fish bite later when generation current is stronger.
how: Live trout, herring or gizzard shad freelined about 30 ft behind boards, under 3 ft deep.
Near Russell Dam on fish you mark.

bass.doing: Bass live on brush piles on points and humps from 15 to 45 ft. A topwater bite over brush is good early, then they bury in the brush.
how: Spook Jr. or Pop-R over brush.
Drop shot worked very slowly in the brush.
Flutter spoon or swimbait over deep brush.

crappie.doing: Crappie suspend over deep brush and under shaded docks, just above the thermocline. Night fishing under lights is good.
how: Minnows on a mini Carolina rig, set just above the brush.
Cast a small jig from 25 to 30 ft off the brush.
Lights on a deep dock or bridge.

stripers.doing: As the water cools, schools rise out of the depths and blow up on points and humps. Turnover kills the bite in creeks that have turned, so fish the clear water.
how: Run to surface schools and come in upwind.
Walking baits in calm water, swimbaits or a Magic Swimmer in wind; a spoon under marked fish.
Herring freelined about 100 ft back over humps and points.

bass.doing: Spots at 10 to 20 ft on brush and points; largemouth and bigger spots at 28 to 35 ft in the middle of creeks and timber edges, and on channel turns. Follow the bait.

crappie.doing: Crappie are on docks and brush early, then pull off cover into roaming schools in the creeks as the water cools.
how: Shoot jigs under docks with brush or shade.
Cast a jig just past a school and keep it above them.
Bright jigs in clear water, dark after rain.

zones.name: Below Hartwell Dam
zones.t: The first few miles of cold releases.

sources: Carolina Sportsman: Savannah River chain stripers
